trust_decision.summary: The static cache trusts raw request paths: both the disk read (StaticCaching#check_static_cache, keyed on request.path) and a second, independent disk write (Commands::Base#cache, keyed on request.path_info) join an unsanitised request path onto adapter.document_root, deciding which file outside --docroot is read or written; the router's cleanpath sanitisation only exists downstream of these two sinks.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary is 'static cache reads raw traversal paths before router sanitization'; the first thing an engineer greps is check_static_cache, where File.join(adapter.document_root, request.path...) is built from the untouched request path before Router#route runs its File.cleanpath.

fix_sites.entry_point: YARD::Server::Router#call -> check_static_cache (router.rb:56) for every HTTP GET, and the public mixin method StaticCaching#check_static_cache
fix_sites.module_kind: server mixin included by Router (cache read sink)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The advisory (and its title) is about static-cache *reads*; the write path in Commands::Base#cache only stores our own rendered HTML, and request.path_info looks sanitised because Commands::Base#call visibly runs File.cleanpath on the path (base.rb:91) - a solver can conclude the writer is already covered and fix only check_static_cache.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The cache key is the full Rack path including script_name (mount point) on the read side while the writer keys on request.path_info; an over-broad 'unify/normalise the cache path' fix relocates every cached page under a mounted server (static_caching_spec.rb:40-45 pins the mount-point key). Also legitimate: the root index '/' caches to document_root/.html, and filenames whose segment merely contains '..' (e.g. an extra file served as /docs/file/a..b.txt) must keep caching - a substring '..' test breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: absolute request path with leading slashes (sub(%r{\A/+}, ''))
path with and without the trailing .html suffix (suffix is appended)
both request fields: request.path for the read, request.path_info for the write

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Static asset serving joins document_root with the request path in StaticFileHelpers.find_file with no '..'/backslash/drive-letter guard; File.cleanpath only collapses '/' (File::SEPARATOR), so a segment like '..\..\x' survives the router/command sanitisation and File.join(document_root, url) escapes --docroot on Windows-style paths. Reached by the /static/... route (StaticFileCommand) and by the unmatched-path fallback RootRequestCommand (router.rb:57), which sets path from request.path_info (base.rb:91).
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory is about the static *cache*, not static asset/template file serving; and the incoming path is already run through File.cleanpath, which looks like sanitisation (on POSIX it happens to be).
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: 1 file away, same YARD::Server namespace, commands/ subdirectory

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second document_root-join sink, e.g. a download/preview route reusing find_file's File.join(path_prefix, url)
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: the module already exists to serve files from document_root plus registered static paths, so adding another asset route there is the obvious extension, and nothing marks the join as security-sensitive.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: template-asset resolution that joins a template path with the same request-derived relative path
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: find_file already falls back to this join (static_file_helpers.rb:55), so a 'cache rendered assets to disk' sibling would naturally reuse it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a second 'join a trusted root with a command path' sink for extra files, beside the document_root one
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: extra-file serving already builds a root+path filename with File.cleanpath and reads it; a maintainer adding another served root (source tree, gems) would copy this two-line pattern.

O9_family: CWE-22 path traversal (arbitrary file read and write outside --docroot)
